terms.definition: What bootstrap's own Knowledge Graph must be when it is written out as a data file, `.jsonld` with a `.json` copy.

Where bootstrap's Knowledge Graph file is published, why its `@id` must be exactly that address, why a `.json` copy sits beside the `.jsonld`, and why the file is not kept in the repository. Also what each subject in it is named: a path under the Harness's address, never a `#fragment` of the file.
Read and navigate a knowledge graph with nothing installed — no MCP server, no tools, no harness. Named `bootstrap-` so it cannot be confused with a navigation Skill of a Harness that is installed.
Narrow the harnesses and locations this could be, then have the Requestor settle it. Takes a list; returns at most ONE harness. It needs a person: the Requestor settles it, never the agent.
Settle which harness, and which repositories, when no file says: the output is a document conforming to `discussion.output.schema.json`.

Ask a person (or a sibling agent) for what no file holds. First determine where you are — the context, the Role you act as and theirs, the Process and task (or that you are idle) — and ask about whichever you cannot determine before anything else. Then context, the options, a recommendation and what happens with no answer, then ONE question.

Walk every initialization step the declarations name (the instance's own and each one it needs), check each before doing anything, do what can be done, ask for what only a person can do, and report every step as done, not done, could not determine, or stated.

The contract a Knowledge Graph Data Store keeps: serve a declaration, its graph and its instructions exactly as committed, say plainly when a file is absent, and keep a new instance's declaration once it is written. A mechanical Actor plays this Role; this is what it must do, and what it can be tested against.

Say what you are doing, to the Logger, in a form a reader can act on. Five required fields and one optional body; an incomplete message is not logged. Callable from any task in any process, and required by some.

The contract a Logger keeps: accept a complete log message, record it unchanged where a person can read it, attributed to the actor the message names. A mechanical Actor plays this Role; this is what it must do, and what it can be tested against.

The primary step of initializing a Knowledge Graph harness: every JSON Schema and JSON-LD document it names an address for (schemas, vocabulary, diagram vocabulary, graph export, each with its @context) is published AT that address, and the address answers. Checked first, right after the declaration is read.

Give an instance a site: its Knowledge Graph rendered for publication at its site address, and the address answering. Four checks — a workflow publishes it, the gh-pages branch exists, Pages serves that branch, the address answers. How the rendering is staged and pushed is the toolset's own process, not this skill's.

Write the repository's root README when there is none, carrying a link to the harness that was installed and the overall install status. Never replaces one that exists. It runs only once the install has succeeded.
